answer: In an agent economy trading opal, nectar, and violet pigments, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before its offers enter buyer searches. The bond stays locked even if the account closes, and each identity gets the same listing quota. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore immobilizes $100,000 for a month; splitting one budget across more names cannot create free listings, so a sybil swarm carries a proportional capital cost.
